F1.caption: Lumen flow rate through the plane nearest z=12 cm. Seven G64 configurations, the 0.0.3 reference and three completed G128/R2 cases are shown. Actual planes are recorded per run in RUN_INVENTORY.json. The dashed IBAMR curve contains the available working-paper samples only (through 0.64 s); it is not extrapolated. G128 changes in stress/solid viscosity/domain length preclude interpretation as an isolated grid-convergence study.

F2.caption: (a) Percentage of lumen points with negative axial velocity on the penultimate exported z plane. (b) Maximum speed over 3.73<r<4.3 cm and all z. Radius is measured about (4.3,4.3). G64 and G128 use their own actual outlet-adjacent planes, listed in the inventory. All 11 retained completed cases are shown.

F3.caption: Minimum local J from solid_stats.csv for G64 P2/R1/R2 and the completed G128/R2 cases. The minimum includes all reported cells, including passive-rim cells, and is sampled at exported times; it is not total solid-volume error. The G64/R2 minimum near 0.89 s is annotated.

F4.caption: Displacement components of two deterministic leaflet-node proxies in the primary G128 run. For AML and PML separately, select the leaflet node with largest absolute axial displacement between t=0 and 0.64 s, then track that same node at every frame. This is not an independently identified anatomical free-edge tip. Candidate IDs and reference positions are in TIP_NODES.json; no trajectory smoothing or favourable-node selection was applied.

F5.caption: Q-criterion iso-surfaces at Q=3956.88 s^-2 for t=0.08,0.16,0.64,0.90 s. The fixed level is 10% of the largest positive-Q 90th percentile across these instants in r<3.5 cm, 2<z<14 cm. Surfaces are clipped to that window and coloured by speed, 0–180 cm/s (values above the limit saturate). Camera and scales are fixed. Leaflets/chordae/caps/annulus are gray; tube and housing disc are omitted. Primary G128/R2 modified-stress run; exploratory numerical fields, not validated vortex topology.

F6.caption: Signed y-vorticity on the centre plane y=4.3 cm at the same four instants, with fixed limits ±620 s^-1. The displayed window is 2<z<14 cm. Derivatives are second-order finite differences of exported point velocities; x-fastest VTK ordering is respected.

F7.caption: Alternative vortex criterion: lambda2=-3580.22 s^-2 iso-surfaces, where lambda2 is the middle eigenvalue of S^2+Omega^2. Same times, spatial window, camera and speed scale as F5. Fixed negative level based on the negative-lambda2 magnitude distribution, as recorded in FIELD_SETTINGS.json.

F8.caption: Instantaneous forward streamlines at t=0.08 and 0.64 s, seeded on a fixed disc at z=7.5 cm, radius 0.15–3.2 cm (6 radial rings, 48 angles). Fourth/fifth-order adaptive Runge–Kutta integration, maximum propagation 30 cm, 3000 steps; initial step 0.05 in VTK default cell-length units. These are instantaneous streamlines, not particle pathlines. Camera/speed scale match F5.

F9.caption: Exterior damping at t=0.30 s. (a) Logarithmic speed map on y=4.3 cm, showing the positive-radial half of the domain. (b) Azimuthal mean speed at z=11.990684 cm. Measured exterior max=0.00215436 cm/s; signed and absolute gap fluxes for 3.8<r<4.3 cm are 0.000131052 and 0.000216216 cm^3/s. These bounds are measured at this time, not imposed or asserted for all times.

F10.caption: Integrated enstrophy (one half of vorticity magnitude squared) and viscous dissipation rate (2 mu S:S), mu=0.04 P. Full Eulerian-box integrals and a lumen window (r<3.5 cm, 2<z<14 cm) are shown, using nodal trapezoidal weights. Full-box values include immersed-solid regions; they are not fluid-only integrals. Boundary transients affect full-box quantities. Exterior contributions are saved separately in energy.csv; no negligible-contribution claim is assumed.

F11.caption: Exploratory summed-component velocity PSD, averaged over fixed probes on z≈8 cm with a 0.5 cm transverse grid inside r<3.5 cm. Welch estimate: 64-sample Hann windows, 50% overlap, mean removal, sampling 100 Hz, Nyquist 50 Hz; final irregular 1.335 s sample omitted. The record is a single nonstationary cycle and does not establish a turbulence spectrum or inertial range.
